contract: issue 620. Rename block b1 of target to new, as seen from referrer. Rust: LinkIndex reads the markdown (extract_links), block_reference_lines names the lines, replace_block_id_refs_to rewrites them. Frontend: renameBlockIdInMarkdown(markdown, target, old, new). Both must produce expected. No ' ^b1' definitions and no ((#^b1)) empty-target self references here: those are each function's own business and are tested apart. No path-qualified targets either (issue 619).

cases.name: a fenced example is not a reference
cases.markdown:
block refs look like this:

```
((note#^b1))
```

and this one is real: ((note#^b1))
cases.expected:
block refs look like this:

```
((note#^b1))
```

and this one is real: ((note#^b2-longer))

cases.name: a code span, and a reference that runs into one
a fence inside a blockquote; four spaces after a list item are a paragraph
an HTML block until the blank line; an inline tag covers only itself
math, an image's alt text and a link reference definition
an embed, a longer new ID and CRLF line endings
table cells are prose, a code span in a cell is not
another file's block with the same ID stays
a byte order mark before the first reference
multibyte text and a combining character around the references
an escape and emphasis inside the display text
nothing to rename is byte-identical
blank-padded inline math, and a pair of dollars that is not a formula to a human
an unclosed display formula runs to the end of the note
a display formula with a blank line inside, and one ended by its blockquote
reference-style images: alt text and label are literal
a dollar inside an inline HTML tag opens no formula
a backtick inside an inline HTML tag opens no code span, so the formula after the tag is a formula
a dollar inside an autolink opens no formula
an escaped dollar opens nothing, the next one does; an escaped backslash leaves the dollar live
